name: Thomas J.
job_title: Principal Data Engineer | Spark | ETL | Python
description:
Principal Data Engineer | Spark | ETL | Python 

I’m a Principal Data Engineer with 13+ years of experience designing and delivering cloud-native, scalable, and secure data platforms, with deep expertise in ETL/ELT pipelines, big data processing, and healthcare data engineering. I specialize in building robust data infrastructure that powers analytics, machine learning, and real-time decision support. 

I led the design and implementation of a HIPAA-compliant, Snowflake-powered healthcare data platform that ingested 3M+ of patient records daily via secure API integrations with diverse EHR, lab, and imaging systems. I built automated mapping to unify medical codes (ICD-10, CPT, LOINC), enforced data quality checks for coding compliance, and implemented schema evolution handling to keep downstream analytics stable. Using Airflow for orchestration, Snowpark/dbt for transformation, and robust encryption for security, I delivered a unified analytics environment that powered AI-driven diagnosis support, real-time clinical decision-making, and population health analytics—reducing manual reconciliation by 90%.

🧩 1. Data Sources & Ingestion Layer 
Healthcare data is fragmented across formats and systems. The ingestion layer had to support: 

Source Systems:
EHRs via FHIR APIs, HL7 v2, and flat files (CSV, XML) 
Lab systems via REST APIs, SFTP uploads, and custom exports 
Payer & billing data via SQL Server / Oracle RDBMS 
Medical devices / IoT through Kafka event streams 

Ingestion Technologies:
- Apache Kafka 
Used for real-time streaming ingestion  
Implemented using Kafka Connect with custom SMTs to normalize topics 

- Apache Airflow (Scheduler) 
DAGs for daily/batch ingestion from APIs, databases 
Used HttpSensor, SimpleHttpOperator, and PythonOperator for API calls 
Used JdbcOperator for legacy RDBMS extraction 

- Custom Python Extractors
requests, pyodbc, cx_Oracle, suds for SOAP/REST integrations 
Decorators for retries, timeouts, logging, and schema validation 
File Watchers 
S3-triggered Lambda and Airflow sensors to detect new lab/EHR batch file drops 

 2. Landing Zone & Raw Storage 

All extracted data landed in Amazon S3 as immutable, timestamped raw snapshots 

Used structured pathing and metadata tagging for lineage 
Organized by source system, entity type (patient, lab, visit), and date 
Compression: Snappy (Avro, Parquet) for efficient Spark processing 

 🔄 3. Data Transformation & Processing Layer

- Apache Spark (PySpark) on EMR / Dataproc 

Parallelized transformation of massive data volumes (~TB-scale per month)
Key transformations included: 
Schema mapping to OMOP CDM 
Deduplication, null handling, type casting 
SCD Type 2 handling for dimension tables 
HL7/FHIR parsing with custom parsers → flattened to relational form 

- Optimization Techniques: 

Partitioning by patient ID, date, and source 
Broadcast joins for small lookup tables
Delta joins with incremental change detection (CDC) where available 
Caching intermediate results where reused in DAGs 

- Data Validation 

Integrated Great Expectations checks into Spark jobs (PySpark wrapper): 
Column nullability 
Value ranges 
Referential integrity between entity tables 
  
🔀 4. Orchestration & Automation 

 - Apache Airflow as the Orchestrator 

Modular DAGs per data domain (e.g., patient, labs, encounters) 
SubDAGs for: 
Extract → Validate → Transform → Load → QA Checks 
Used dynamic DAG generation based on config files (YAML/JSON) per source 
Alerting via Slack, PagerDuty, and email for SLA breaches 

- CI/CD Automation 

GitHub Actions for: 
Airflow DAG deployment 
PySpark job packaging 
Terraform-based infra updates 

🗄️ 5. Load into Central Warehouse 
After transformation, curated and standardized data was loaded into a cloud-native warehouse: 

- Options depending on client: 

Snowflake – for ad hoc query workloads and time-travel 
AWS Redshift – for cheaper, high-throughput warehouse workloads
Google BigQuery – for serverless scale and ML integrations 

- Load Design: 

Used MERGE/UPSERT patterns 
Partitioned by encounter date, organization ID, or region 
Maintained audit logs and row-level lineage using ETL metadata tables 

📊 6. Downstream Access & Visualization 
- BI / Analytics Consumers: 

Tableau, Power BI, and Looker users querying defined data marts 
ML engineers pulling features from curated tables for predictive models 
Regulatory teams using the platform for HIPAA, CMS, and MACRA reporting 
 
- Enablement Strategy: 

Created semantic views and marts 
Maintained Data Dictionary and Entity Relationship Diagrams (ERDs) 
Used dbt for analytics engineering, versioned SQL transformations, and documentation 

- Performance & Scalability

Throughput: Ingested and processed 10M+ records per day 
Pipeline runtime: Reduced full refresh from 18 hours → <1 hour (parallel DAGs) 
Data freshness: Achieved sub-hour latency for critical domains 
Scalability: Spark autoscaling with adaptive query execution for burst handling
